verdict: NVR's revenue fell 8% to $2.4B and profit fell 27% to $249M as home settlements dropped and lot costs and pricing pressure squeezed margins.

segments.name: Homebuilding
segments.note: Selling and building homes (Ryan Homes, NVHomes, Heartland Homes) — down 8% as settlements fell 7% to 5,268 homes.

segments.name: Mortgage banking fees
segments.note: Fees from mortgage banking for home buyers — mortgage segment profit rose to $35M despite loan production falling 10%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Homebuilding SG&A of $135M plus mortgage banking general and administrative costs of $23M.

otherDetail: Other is about $11M net: homebuilding other income $12M and mortgage interest and other income $5M, less homebuilding and mortgage interest expense of about $7M. Figures are rounded to $M; reported net income was $248.6M.
footerNote: Consolidated revenue is homebuilding revenues ($2,349M) plus mortgage banking fees ($53M), as in NVR's 10-Q ($2,402M). Cost of revenue is homebuilding cost of sales; mortgage fees have no cost of sales, so the consolidated gross margin differs from the 18.3% homebuilding gross margin. Contract land deposit impairments were about $24.8M inside the quarter's costs.
oneTimers: Contract land deposit impairments totalled approximately $24.8M in the quarter, hurting homebuilding gross margin.

takeaways.title: Settlements fell
takeaways.text: Home settlements fell 7% to 5,268 and the average settlement price fell 2%, taking homebuilding revenue down 8%.

takeaways.title: Margins squeezed
takeaways.text: Homebuilding gross margin fell to 18.3% from 21.0% on higher lot costs, pricing pressure and $24.8M of land deposit impairments.

takeaways.title: Cancellations rose
takeaways.text: The new-order cancellation rate rose to 21% from 19%, and new orders fell 7% to 4,391 — demand stayed soft.
